stories.title: Sports roundup: CAF makes Kiswahili an official language, Liverpool thrash 10-man Man United
key_points: CAF voted in Abuja to make Kiswahili its fifth official language, ahead of AFCON 2027 in East Africa.
Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as United boss.
Harambee Stars coach Benni McCarthy complained about poor hotel and meals in South Africa.
Brentford v Everton closes the Premier League round on Monday night (8pm UK time).
stories.content:
Here is the weekend's sports news, with a big win for East Africa at the top.

Kiswahili becomes an official language of African football

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has made Kiswahili one of its official languages. The vote happened at CAF's 48th Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday, November 21, with all 54 member countries represented, KBC and P.M. News reported.

Kiswahili now joins English, French, Arabic and Portuguese. CAF said the move shows respect for Africa's many languages.

Why it matters: Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda will co-host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON). Kiswahili is spoken by more than 200 million people across East, Central and Southern Africa, according to HapaKenya.

At the same meeting, CAF reported a profit of $31.2 million on revenue of about $284 million for its 2026 financial year, and backed FIFA President Gianni Infantino for re-election, Freedom Online reported.

Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United manager ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield on Sunday.

  • United defender Leny Yoro was sent off after 8 minutes.
  • Dominik Szoboszlai (10') and Florian Wirtz (13') scored quickly for Liverpool.
  • Teenager Rio Ngumoha (66') and substitute Victor Munoz (82') added two more.

The loss keeps United in the relegation zone, one point above the bottom, Sky Sports reported.

Other Premier League results this weekend

  • Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal
  • Chelsea 1-4 Leeds
  • Manchester City 1-1 Fulham
  • Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich
  • Bournemouth 2-0 Nottingham Forest
  • Coventry 3-2 Crystal Palace
  • Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland
  • Hull 2-0 Brighton

Brentford host Everton on Monday night to close the round.

Harambee Stars: coach speaks out

Kenya's national team lost 2-1 to South Africa at Nyayo Stadium in Nairobi on November 17 in an AFCON qualifier, The Star reported. Relebohile Mofokeng scored twice for South Africa and Mohamed Bajaber got a late goal for Kenya.

Coach Benni McCarthy later said the team's hotel and meals during the trip to Johannesburg were below standard, and that the squad could not even fly home together, the Nation reported. Kenya has already qualified for AFCON 2027 as a co-host.

stories.title: World roundup: COP31 ends without a deal, Iran tensions stay high, Russia steps up attacks on Ukraine
key_points: UN climate talks in Turkey ended Sunday with no main agreement; COP32 goes to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
Fighting between the US and Iran has returned; Trump says he wants a lasting deal.
Zelenskyy asked the US to release Patriot missiles after a week of heavy Russian attacks.
UN peacekeepers in Lebanon are handing their work to the Lebanese army before their mission ends.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the weekend, in short and simple form.

1. Climate talks end with no main deal

The UN climate summit, COP31, ended in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday, November 22, without the main agreement countries were working on, UN News reported. Talks ran two days past the deadline, making it the longest UN climate summit on record.

The big fight was over coal, oil and gas. Countries hit hard by climate change wanted a clear plan to move away from fossil fuels. Big fuel exporters, such as Saudi Arabia and Russia, pushed back, CBS News and other outlets reported. The European Union, Panama and the Marshall Islands rejected the final text.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the result a deep disappointment. Ghana, speaking for the African Group, said the text fell short on money for poorer countries but did not block it.

Why it matters for Africa: the next summit, COP32, will be held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and will take up the unfinished issues.

2. US–Iran: fighting is back, talk of a deal continues

The US–Iran conflict began on February 28, 2026. A ceasefire and a June agreement followed, but that agreement broke down and fighting returned, Gulf News reported. The two sides exchanged fire again on November 17.

President Donald Trump said the US is talking to Iran and wants a deal that lasts even after he leaves office. He has not shared a plan or a timetable. Meanwhile, Anadolu Agency reported that Bahrain renewed its threat alert, after Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they had destroyed two US radar systems there. That claim has not been independently confirmed.

3. Ukraine asks for more air defence

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged the United States to approve the delivery of Patriot missiles, which can shoot down ballistic missiles, Al Jazeera reported. He said partners have already paid for them.

Zelenskyy said Russia fired about 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 guided bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine in one week. On Sunday, a Russian drone attack partly brought down an apartment building in Dymer, near Kyiv, and rescuers were searching for missing people, including children.

4. UN peacekeepers prepare to leave Lebanon

The UN force in southern Lebanon, UNIFIL, has begun handing its duties to the Lebanese army, according to Anadolu Agency. The UN Security Council voted in 2025 to end the mission on December 31, 2026, with troops leaving during 2027. Lebanese leaders have asked for more time, so far without success, the Associated Press reported.

stories.title: Sifuna's US tour reaches Pennsylvania as Kenyan politicians chase diaspora money and support
key_points: Sifuna landed at Newark, New Jersey, to a lively welcome from Kenyans waving flags.
Sunday's plan: church at Grace Community Church, then a town hall at The Palace Center, Allentown.
Next stops: Maryland and the Washington DC area from Nov 23.
Analysts say US tours are mostly about raising campaign money.
stories.content:
ALLENTOWN, Pennsylvania — Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's tour of the United States moved to Pennsylvania on Sunday, November 22, the second day of a 17-day trip to meet Kenyans living in America.

Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) and has said he will run for president in Kenya's August 2027 election.

A warm welcome

Sifuna landed at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, where dozens of Kenyans waved flags and chanted as his team arrived, Uzalendo News reported. The Star said supporters broke into song and dance when they saw him.

He is travelling with Vihiga Senator Godfrey Osotsi and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, according to The Star.

The tour's plan was to open an LMM office in Hackettstown, New Jersey, at noon on Saturday, November 21.

Sunday in Allentown

The published programme for Sunday was:

  • a morning church service at Grace Community Church in Allentown;
  • a town hall meeting at The Palace Center, from 2pm to 6pm.

KASS-mtv had not yet seen reports of what was said at the town hall when this story was written. We will update readers when we do.

Where the tour goes next

  • Nov 23–25: Maryland and the Washington DC area — community dinner, policy meeting, women's brunch, Gen Z meeting and a town hall;
  • Late November: Dallas and Houston, Texas;
  • Early December: Seattle and California, ending on December 7.

Dates have changed before, so check with the organisers before you travel.

Why politicians keep coming to the US

Sifuna is not the first. Democracy for the Citizens Party leader Rigathi Gachagua made a long US tour earlier this year, with stops that included Oregon, Kansas, Dallas, Boston and Spokane, the Nation reported. The Star reported that Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka is also planning a US tour.

Analysts say money is a big reason. Political analyst Martin Andati told The Star the tours are mainly about fundraising, because the number of Kenyans living abroad is small compared with voters at home. Prof Kefa Otiso of Bowling Green State University told the Nation that the diaspora also helps politicians by persuading family and friends back home.

The money Kenyans in the US send home

Kenyans in the US are the country's biggest source of money sent home, but that flow has slowed this year. Central Bank of Kenya Governor Kamau Thugge said total remittances fell 1.3% in the 12 months to August 2026, mostly because less money came from the US and Saudi Arabia, Kenyans.co.ke reported. Kenyans.co.ke has also linked part of the slowdown to a new US tax on money transfers.

According to The Rio Times, citing CBK figures, money from the US in October 2026 was about US$178 million, 28% lower than a year earlier.

For Kenyans in America, that makes the coming town halls a chance to ask candidates direct questions about jobs, remittance costs and how the diaspora can vote.

stories.title: Opposition leaders reject 'third force' talk as Gachagua promises Mt Kenya direction before Christmas
key_points: Matiang'i, Nyoro and Karua told a Kirinyaga church on Sunday that the opposition is one team.
They said the opposition will field one presidential candidate, but gave no date or method.
In Embu, Gachagua said he will give Mt Kenya its political direction before Christmas.
Gachagua also asked the IEBC to say when the voter register will be audited.
stories.content:
NAIROBI — Three opposition leaders used a church service in Kirinyaga on Sunday, November 22, to deny reports that they are building a separate "third force" inside the opposition.

At the same time, in neighbouring Embu County, former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua held his own church meeting and set out his plans for the Mt Kenya vote.

What happened in Kirinyaga

Jubilee Party leader Fred Matiang'i, People's Party of Kenya (PPK) leader Ndindi Nyoro and People's Liberation Party (PLP) leader Martha Karua attended a service at Kimunye ACK Church, The Star reported. Kirinyaga is Ms Karua's home county. MPs Anthony Kibagendi (Kitutu South), Clive Gisairo (Kitutu Masaba) and Patrick Osero (Borabu) were also there.

The four leaders, together with Siaya Governor James Orengo, have toured several regions together in recent weeks, including Gusii. The Nation reported that this had fuelled talk of a new power bloc that could shape who the opposition picks as its presidential candidate.

The leaders said that is not true:

  • Nyoro said, according to The Star: "There is only one force in the Opposition." He said the opposition will pick one flagbearer, and that leaders missing from Kirinyaga were meeting supporters in Embu and other places.
  • Matiang'i said the opposition has no time for fighting and accused unnamed people of trying to divide it for their own gain. "We have one team in Kenya in the opposition," he said, as quoted by The Kenya Times.
  • Karua said the leaders' different tours are planned together to win support across the country, and that the opposition will settle on one candidate to face President William Ruto.

According to The Kenya Times, Ms Karua has also said she is ready to step aside and back either Matiang'i or Nyoro if the opposition chooses one of them. The opposition has not yet said how or when it will pick its candidate.

What Gachagua said in Embu

Mr Gachagua, who leads the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), spoke at Wonders of God Church in Karurumo, Runyenjes, People Daily reported. He said:

  • he will give the Mt Kenya region its political direction before Christmas, after months of meetings with residents. The Kenya Times reported the dates as December 22 or 23;
  • families can use the holidays to discuss and agree on the region's preferred candidates;
  • the IEBC should say when it will audit the voter register, and remove dead voters and foreigners he claims are on it. People Daily noted he did not give evidence for the claim about foreigners.

Citizen Digital reported that Mr Gachagua also said opposition leaders now hold key voting regions, naming Mt Kenya for himself, Kisii for Matiang'i and Lower Eastern for Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka.

Why it matters

Kenya's next general election is in August 2027. The opposition has many leaders who want to run for president, and every one of them says the group will back a single candidate. How they choose that person is the big question for the coming months.

The IEBC had not publicly responded to Mr Gachagua's demands by the time of writing.

stories.title: Sifuna brings Linda Mwananchi tour to Kenyans in the US, starting Saturday in New Jersey
key_points: The tour starts Saturday, Nov 21, in Hackettstown, New Jersey, and ends Dec 7 in Silicon Valley, California.
Stops include Pennsylvania, Maryland, Washington DC, Texas, Seattle and California.
Plans include town halls, community dinners and meetings with Gen Z groups.
The dates have changed before, so check with the organisers before you travel.
stories.content:
Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna is taking his Linda Mwananchi Movement to Kenyans in the United States, with a tour that starts this Saturday in New Jersey.

The movement says the tour will open on November 21 with a new Linda Mwananchi office in Hackettstown, New Jersey, at noon, and end in Silicon Valley, California, on December 7.

Where and when (latest published plan)

  • Nov 21, Hackettstown, NJ: office opening at noon
  • Nov 22, Allentown, PA: church service, then a town hall at Palace Center from 2pm to 6pm
  • Nov 23, Maryland: community dinner at Spark Hotel at 7:30pm
  • Nov 24, Washington, DC
  • Nov 27, Dallas, TX
  • Nov 29, Houston, TX
  • Dec 3–4, Seattle area, WA: Renton and Federal Way
  • Dec 5, San Francisco and Oakland, CA
  • Dec 7, Silicon Valley, CA

The plan includes town hall meetings, community dinners, sessions with Gen Z groups and meetings with elected officials, Capital FM reported.

Earlier versions of the schedule were different. A programme reported by the Nation and The Standard in early November had Sifuna arriving in Allentown on November 20 and finishing in Seattle and California by December 4. Please confirm times and venues with the organisers before travelling.

Why the tour matters

Sifuna is seen as a rising challenger to President William Ruto ahead of the August 2027 election. The Nation reported that the trip aims to win over diaspora voters and raise money for his campaign.

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua made a similar US trip from August 26 to October 9, with stops including Spokane, Portland, Kansas, Dallas and Boston.

The visit also comes as the money Kenyans abroad send home is slowing down:

  • October: Central Bank of Kenya figures show remittances were $430.5 million in October 2026, down 1.9% from October 2025.
  • 12 months to October: remittances fell 1.1% to $5.023 billion.
  • From the US: money from Kenya's biggest source fell 12.6% in the first half of the year, according to Business Daily. A new US tax on money transfers began on January 1.

stories.title: Ruto starts 8-day Western Kenya tour as poll shows Sifuna ahead in the region
key_points: Ruto is touring all four Western counties: Busia, Kakamega, Vihiga and Bungoma.
A Tifa poll last week put Senator Edwin Sifuna at 55% in Western, against Ruto's 25%.
Ruto launched roads, markets, a cultural centre and electricity connections.
Kenya's next general election is in August 2027.
stories.content:
NAIROBI — President William Ruto has begun an eight-day campaign tour of Western Kenya, a region where a new poll shows Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna well ahead of him.

The tour covers all four Western counties — Busia, Kakamega, Vihiga and Bungoma — and is split into two parts, with rest days in between, The Star reported on Friday.

On Thursday, Ruto was in Busia and Bungoma. In Teso North, Busia, he:

  • opened the Kakapel Cultural Centre;
  • opened new classrooms and offices at Kapkemer Comprehensive Primary School;
  • launched work on the Butula–Nambale–Amukura–Machakusi–Kocholia road;
  • started the Last Mile electricity connection project at Segero Centre.

In Bungoma, he launched two road projects, laid the foundation stone for Bokoli Modern Market and opened Naitiri Modern Market in Tongaren.

On Friday he was due in Budalang'i and Funyula in Busia, then Butere and Shinyalu in Kakamega. Saturday's plan includes Matungu, Sirisia and Vihiga.

Why Western matters now

The trip comes a week after a Tifa poll found 55% support for Sifuna in Western, against 25% for Ruto. Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement and is seen as a growing challenger ahead of the 2027 election.

Western has long voted with the late Raila Odinga. Ruto had been expected to win much of that support through his working deal with ODM, but Sifuna's rise has changed the picture. Ruto also needs Western votes to make up for support he may lose in Mt Kenya after his split with former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua.

Speaking in Teso North, Ruto accused his rivals of dividing people along tribal lines and said they have no plans for schools, electricity, roads or health. "Those people, we shall show them dust in the elections," he said.

Several leaders joined him:

  • Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi;
  • National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula;
  • Cooperatives Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya;
  • Busia Governor Paul Otuoma.

Oparanya said ODM remains in the broad-based government and will back Ruto's re-election. Wetang'ula urged a big turnout in August next year.

According to The Star, Ruto has visited about 24 counties in the past two months.

KASS-mtv will follow the rest of the tour.
